about: Block Square on a sale night: what stands where, who is there, what they say and what is called from the Block. Read by Tools/build_town_level.py (GUT_TOWN_LIST=Tools/town_block_square.json Tools/build_town_level.sh). Places are in the map's own metres (x east, y north), from for-review/design/map-of-ashmarket.md; 'yaw' and 'facing' are compass bearings (0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west). STAGE 2: the Block's trailer, its lamps, the ramp, the tables, the scale, the rope, the Holding Yard's truck beds and the counting house are models made in Mixar for it (ArtSource/mixar/square_*), and its board, bills and marks are pictures made there.
name: Block Square
errand: The Block is selling. The way in is the gap in the rope.
To buy a fighter: Margin, at the table.
To borrow or pay: Mother Ledger.
Back to the Gut: north, up the lane.
walk_about: The ground that can be walked on. Each patch runs on into whatever stands along its edge (a wall, a row of containers, a fence), and that is what stops whoever walks: the builder measures every model and refuses a place where a patch ends at nothing.
rows_about: Containers end to end, stacked. 'face' is the line their near sides stand on, 'side' the side of it they lie on, and they are spread between 'from' and 'to'. The blue one's awning is on its own left, so 'yaw' is chosen to turn it to the street.

people.name: Margin
people.prompt: Talk to Margin, the Block's clerk

lines.words: Lot list is on the board. If you are buying, I write your name against theirs, and they sleep in your yard tonight. The Chainmen's fifth is in the price already. Are you buying?

answers.words: Show me who is for sale.

lines.words: Eighteen litres, and six more for each thing they know how to do, before anybody bids. A fighter with a name costs what the Gut says they cost.
{dealt} Your page says {owed} litres owed, and you are holding {held}. I lend twenty-five and I write thirty-five. I like to begin with the figures.

answers.words: Take what I owe out of what I hold.

lines.words: People who signed. I have never collared anybody. People sign. I only remember it for them.
Main Street is shut below the square until the last lot is down. You want the gate, you wait like everybody else.

doors.prompt: Up the lane to Pool Street
Look through the Holding Yard's fence
doors.shut: Chain-link backed with road signs, three and a half metres of it. The lots come up from the other side.

calls_about: What Caller Strand calls from the Block, round and round. Nobody speaks it: there is no voice for it, so it is written up on the screen. 'stirs' is a lot knocked down, which gets something out of the crowd. Prices follow the numbers pass: 18 L and 6 L for each skill, before bidding.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot one. A man, twenty-six, sound in wind and limb. Digs, hauls, and has swung a club for money.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty litres opens. Thirty. Who starts me?

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty at the rope. Thirty-five, the Gut's man. Forty, at the back.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Forty-five? Forty-five, Mr Rask. Going at forty-five.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Forty-five litres, to Mr Rask of the Gut.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot one, forty-five litres, to H. Rask. Nine to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot two. A woman, thirty-one. Reads, figures, and sews a straight seam. Three things on the card.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty-six opens, and cheap at it. Thirty-six, the Tin. Forty.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Forty-four, the Pump office. Forty-eight, the Tin again. Any more?

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Forty-eight litres, to the Velvet Tin.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot two, forty-eight litres, to the Tin. Nine and a half to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot three. A man, nineteen. Strong as he looks and knows nothing yet. Somebody will teach him.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Eighteen opens. Eighteen, the Scrappers. Twenty.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Twenty-two. Twenty-two once. Nobody? He eats less than a dog.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Twenty-two litres, to the Scrappers' guild.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot three, twenty-two litres, to the guild. Four and a half to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot four. A woman, twenty-four. Cooks, and can strip a pump and put it back. Two on the card.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty opens. Thirty, the Pump office. Thirty-four, at the rope.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty-eight, the Pump. Forty-two. Forty-two, and the Pump shakes its head.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Forty-two litres, to the bidder at the rope.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot four, forty-two litres. Name, please. Eight and a half to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot five. A man, thirty-five, heavy. Hauls for two and has stood in a ring and walked out of it.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty opens. Thirty-five, Mr Rask. Forty, the Scrappers.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Forty-five, Mr Rask. Fifty. Fifty, Mr Rask, and that is the Gut's water talking.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Fifty litres, to Mr Rask of the Gut.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot five, fifty litres, to H. Rask. Ten to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot six. A woman, twenty-eight. Reads, and keeps a count. Signed for her brother's water and here she stands.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty opens. Thirty, the Tin. Thirty-four, the Pump office.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty-eight? Thirty-eight, the Pump. Going at thirty-eight.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Thirty-eight litres, to the Pump office.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot six, thirty-eight litres, to the Pump. Seven and a half to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: That is the six. Hold your water: the next six are at the wash, and they come up when they are clean.
